mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign shareholder (e.g., ACRA, Companies House, or equivalent registrar)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize a certified copy in the origin state; if the origin state is party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, obtain a single Apostille from the designated Competent Authority and submit to Chinese authorities without consular legalization. If the origin state is not an Apostille member, obtain notarization and then consular legalization from the Embassy/Consulate of the People's Republic of China only; the Apostille and consular paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Active Status of the Ultimate Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Genuine company registry or registrar of companies in the foreign shareholder's state of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain a dated certificate from the competent registrar. For Apostille Convention states, affix the Hague Apostille through the competent authority and do not add Chinese consular legalization. For non-member states, follow notarization plus Chinese consular legalization only. Never combine Apostille and consular legalization in sequential form.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation of the WFOE, capital contribution, and execution of constitutional documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign corporate shareholder as certified by its corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Have the resolution notarized in the origin country, then obtain a Hague Apostille if the origin country is a party to the Apostille Convention. If the origin country is not a party, complete consular legalization at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate having territorial jurisdiction. The two authentication methods are mutually exclusive and must not be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of the Ultimate Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or registered agent of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certify the copy by a local notary, then either obtain a Hague Apostille from the competent authority of an Apostille member state or, if the issuing state is not a member, obtain Chinese consular legalization. Use only one path per document; do not sequence Apostille after consular legalization or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Ultimate Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate or correspondent bank maintaining the foreign shareholder's settlement account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank issues the letter on letterhead; the issuing officer's signature is notarized in the origin country. The notarized document then takes only the Hague Apostille path if the origin country is an Apostille party, or the consular legalization path only if it is not. Both paths remain exclusive and parallel.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening must cover all UBOs, directors, legal representatives and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, OFAC Sectoral Sanctions Identifications List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, PRC domestic anti-money-laundering watchlists, and PEP databases. Adverse media searches must be refreshed before bank account opening, before each Swift wire and escrow release, and continuously for at least 90 days. All hits must be escalated to the AML compliance officer, subject to independent second-person review, and documented in a Board-approved AML risk file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Independent Declaration and Registration Portal through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A WFOE name must follow the mandatory four-tier structure: (i) administrative division; (ii) distinctive trade name in simplified Chinese; (iii) industry or operating characteristic relevant to aircraft engine leasing; and (iv) company form such as Limited Company. The distinctive portion must be simplified Chinese script; if a foreign name is used, it must be phonetically transliterated into Chinese and used only alongside the registered Chinese name. Name tokens must not violate national security, public interest, or social morality, and must not mislead as to the enterprise's legal or ownership structure.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On name rejection, the applicant may submit an administrative reconsideration application to the SAMR that approved the name or to its superior authority within 15 working days of receiving the written rejection. The application must contain the proposed Chinese name, the rejection notice, a legal memorandum demonstrating compliance with the four-tier naming rules, and any ministerial consent. If reconsideration fails, an administrative lawsuit may be filed in the competent people's court within 6 months of the reconsideration decision, and the applicant may simultaneously reserve a backup name for continuity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a WFOE conducting aircraft engine dry leasing, a pure virtual office or post-office-box address is not acceptable to the SAMR, the local taxation authority, or a Chinese bank for opening a basic settlement account. The registered address must be a physical place of management that can receive official mail, retain books and records, and accommodate on-site inspection. A shared workspace may be accepted only if the space is under a written lease in the WFOE's name, separate workstations exist, and the landlord provides an occupancy certificate; otherwise the VAT registration and bank account opening will be rejected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood: approximately 35-45% for a newly registered WFOE within the first 12 months if the registered address is shared or in a virtual office cluster; above 80% if the address is flagged as a high-risk concentration address. Checklist: verify physical door plate, lease agreement, payment receipts for utilities, staff on site, accounting ledger availability, VAT invoice system, and bank correspondence; ensure the tax officer's unannounced visit can be satisfied within 15 minutes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 23-36, 43-50 and 96-102; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 12, 28 and 30; Measures for the Administration of Market Entity Registration of the State Administration for Market Regulation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Municipal Market Regulation Administration (SAMR) where the registered office is located, operating under the State Administration for Market Regulation.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company together with the approved Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The 2023 Company Law imposes no uniform minimum paid-up capital for ordinary limited liability companies. For this wholly foreign-owned enterprise, the statutory minimum is zero for the aircraft engine dry leasing scope. Registered capital must be subscribed in an amount reasonably commensurate with proposed business operations and paid in full within five years from the date of issuance of the business license unless the shareholders agree on an earlier schedule. No escrow or blocked account is required by law; a bank may, however, require an earmarked capital account where lease finance or loan covenants call for custodial arrangements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD, a wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company organized under the laws of the People's Republic of China. Date: [DATE]; Venue: [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS]; Attendance: all directors named in the Articles of Association, together with an appointed corporate secretary; quorum duly certified. The board received unanimous written consent from the sole foreign shareholder to incorporate the company, adopt the Articles of Association, and approve the initial corporate governance arrangements. After due deliberation, the following resolutions were passed by unanimous vote. 1. Share Capital Subscription. The board confirms that the registered capital of the company is [AMOUNT] RMB, divided into [NUMBER] capital interests, subscribed by the shareholder. Pursuant to the 2023 Company Law and the Foreign Investment Law, the board approves the capital contribution schedule and directs the legal representative to execute subscription receipts and collect capital contributions through lawful banking channels. 2. Banking Authorization. The board authorizes the opening of RMB and foreign currency bank accounts at [BANK NAME], and designates the general manager and chief financial officer as joint signatories, with authority to execute account documents, wire transfer instructions, escrow agreements, and lease finance undertakings. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The board adopts [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS] as the registered office and ratifies the lease agreement, directing the corporate secretary to make all required registry, tax, and statutory filings. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The board appoints [NAME] as legal representative and executive director, [NAME] as chief financial officer, and [NAME] as supervisor, each for a term of three years. The officers are authorized and duty-bound to operate within the approved scope of aircraft engine dry leasing, ISIC 5223/NAICS 532411, and to ensure continuous compliance with corporate governance, anti-money laundering, customs, and tax obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the WFOE legal name and business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Regulation Administration online enterprise name registration portal under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation through the official enterprise registration service. The applicant must state one primary and two backup legal names in Chinese, specify the intended scope as aircraft engine dry leasing and auxiliary aviation support services, and declare the proposed registered capital. The system automatically screens for duplicates, prohibited names, and unfair competition risks. The authority will issue a Name Reservation Notice valid for six months. The application should be prepared in Chinese with an English summary; if the name is queried, the applicant must explain the commercial rationale and submit revised candidates within the notice window.
required_dossiers: Primary and alternate legal names
Stated business scope ISIC 5223 / NAICS 532411
Shareholder identity documents
Proposed directors and supervisor identity documents
Registered office address commitment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the reserved name is refused or suspended, file a revised name application with new candidate names, or lodge an administrative reconsideration petition with the higher-level Market Regulation Administration within 60 days of the written refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Authenticate foreign investor documents and file incorporation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Regulation Administration service hall or integrated online registration system under SAMR.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign shareholder's certificate of incorporation and director identity documents must be notarized in the home jurisdiction and either apostilled or legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate in accordance with the Hague Apostille Convention of 2023. The Chinese law firm or authorized agent will prepare the Articles of Association, shareholder resolution, director appointment letters, and lease agreement. Submit the full dossier to the local Market Regulation Administration through the integrated enterprise registration platform or at the service hall. The examiner will verify that the proposed legal representative, corporate governance structure, and foreign investment negative list status are lawful. The entire filing should be completed without payment of a national registration fee; local practice may charge a nominal document-processing fee.
required_dossiers: Notarized and legalized foreign shareholder incorporation certificate
Power of attorney to the authorized representative
Consent letters of directors and supervisor
Articles of Association signed by shareholder and directors
Board resolution and minutes of formation
Lease agreement or registered address certificate
Approved Name Reservation Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension, respond with corrected forms and supplementary evidence within 15 working days; if the rejection relates to foreign investment negative list interpretation, obtain a pre-filing opinion from the local commerce authority and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain business license and corporate seals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Regulation Administration and a registered seal engraving enterprise approved by the Public Security Bureau.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the incorporation registration is approved, SAMR issues the Business License containing the Unified Social Credit Code. The legal representative should collect the license in person or authorize an agent with a notarized power of attorney. Immediately thereafter, the company shall engage a licensed seal engraving enterprise to produce the company seal, finance seal, contract seal, legal representative seal, and invoice seal. The engraving enterprise will submit seal impressions to the Public Security Bureau for filing, and the filing receipt is required for opening bank accounts and issuing invoices. Preserve the original license and seal filing certificate together with the company constitution for inspection by banks and tax authorities.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Notice
Business License application receipt
Legal representative passport or national identity document
Agent power of attorney, if applicable
Company seal engraving application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If business license issuance is delayed, request the examiner's written notice of additional requirements and respond within the statutory deadline; if seal filing is refused because the requested seal type exceeds statutory scope, adjust the seal set and re-apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate tax registration, foreign exchange capital account, and labor registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration local office, a commercial bank authorized for foreign direct investment settlement, and municipal social insurance and housing fund authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The new WFOE is automatically notified to the tax authority but must complete its tax registration confirmation online, select the accounting standards, and apply for general taxpayer status if appropriate. A basic settlement account in RMB and a foreign exchange capital account should be opened at a bank authorized by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE). The board resolution and seal filing certificate are required for the account signing matrix. The company must also register employers and employees with social insurance and housing fund systems; any delay creates penalties. Foreign investor capital may then be remitted and converted for operational use under the Foreign Investment Law, provided that the bank records the amount in the FDI information system.
required_dossiers: Business License
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Articles of Association and board resolution
Corporate seal, finance seal, and legal representative seal
Lease contract and bank opening forms
Foreign exchange registration information form
Statutory officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is blocked due to address discrepancies, submit the updated lease and a declaration from the registered owner; if the bank delays the foreign exchange capital account, escalate to the SAFE local branch with the FDI payment declaration and a rectification undertaking.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete aviation, customs, and post-formation statutory filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil Aviation Administration of China regional administration, General Administration of Customs, and optional Free Trade Zone administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Dry leasing of aircraft engines is an asset-heavy service without air carrier operations, so no Air Operator Certificate is required. If engines are leased to carriers in the People's Republic of China, the WFOE should file a written equipment leasing notice to the CAAC regional office so that the engine registration and lease agreement in compliance with international civil aviation standards. If engines cross the border, the company must register as a customs importer/exporter, obtain an HS classification for the relevant engine type, and comply with general trade or special customs surveillance. For finance-lease structures, the tax authority may require value-added tax filings on lease payments. The board should ensure that AML enhanced due diligence controls for aviation leasing are documented in the compliance manual.
required_dossiers: Business License
CAAC equipment lease notice
Customs registration form and HS classification
Lease agreements and maintenance management contracts
Anti-money laundering compliance manual
Tax registration certificate and VAT filing profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CAAC or customs authority asks for supplemental information, provide legal opinions and engine technical specifications; if a lease transaction is suspended, seek a written ruling from the relevant bureau or file an administrative reconsideration within the prescribed period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - this WFOE performs no manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing; no industrial licensing board clearance is required at formation. If the company later establishes an engine maintenance or storage facility, the local Market Regulation Administration and the Ministry of Emergency Management would become the relevant authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating permit is required for ISIC 5223 dry leasing of turbofan aircraft engines; the ordinary business license authorises the leasing activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China (MEE) and its provincial/city-level local bureaus.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no construction of production facilities, no land development, no stationary discharge points, and no hazardous waste generation. The activity is limited to contractual leasing of aircraft engines, and therefore no EIA report, environmental impact statement, or environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No quantitative thresholds for wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste apply because the WFOE does not operate an industrial installation. If an administrative office only is maintained, domestic sewage is discharged to municipal networks subject to local water pollutant discharge standards, not an EIA permit. If the entity stores aviation fuel or engine lubricants in quantities above 1 cubic meter, it must obtain an MEE hazardous-waste management record and comply with the ambient air quality VOC limits in the applicable local standard.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office-only facility: the building owner's fire safety inspection certificate and a fire safety self-inspection record suffice; no Civil Defense fire permit is required because there is no manufacturing storage or processing area. Workplace safety is limited to general obligations under the Work Safety Law, including emergency exit maintenance and employee safety training. If the WFOE later establishes a hangar or maintenance workshop, it must apply for planning approval, fire protection design review, completion fire acceptance from the local Fire and Rescue Department, and register the workplace with the relevant occupational safety regulatory body.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; administrative filings and registrations are processed through the nationwide Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) online portal operated by STA, with taxpayer service supported by the 12366 tax service hotline.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the newly established Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE), the foreign shareholder first incorporates the entity through the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) national enterprise registration system; the issued business license contains the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which automatically constitutes the WFOE's taxpayer identification number (TIN) for corporate income tax and VAT. Within 30 days of issuance, the legal representative or authorised tax agent must complete tax registration in the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax), confirming the primary tax authority, tax filing period, and subject classification. For VAT purposes, the WFOE must classify itself as a small-scale taxpayer or a general VAT taxpayer; if cumulative taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 in any rolling 12-month period, general taxpayer registration is mandatory, while below the threshold general taxpayer registration may be elected where the statutory conditions are met. The WFOE then registers for electronic invoice issuance through the STA e-invoice service platform or an STA-certified e-invoicing API, obtains its e-invoice quota, and begins real-time digital invoice transmission. For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a Chinese establishment or place of business that leases aircraft engines into China and derives Chinese-source lease income subject to withholding, the non-resident enterprise must complete a separate tax registration with the local STA sub-bureau where the payer or withholding agent is located; STA assigns a dedicated non-resident enterprise TIN for corporate income tax withholding and VAT obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise subject to Corporate Income Tax at 25% on worldwide income; no pass-through or flow-through treatment is available, and it is not treated as a territorially exempt or tax-holiday entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None available for entity classification. PRC tax law does not provide a check-the-box, partnership-style transparency election, hybrid mismatch election, or tax consolidation election for a WFOE limited liability company. The only administrative elections are the VAT small-scale taxpayer versus general taxpayer election, and the simplified taxation election for certain prescribed services where specifically authorised by STA circulars; there is no election to alter the entity-level tax character of the WFOE.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) of the People's Republic of China; for the aircraft-engine dry-leasing business, operating leasing of tangible movable property is chargeable at the standard VAT rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration is triggered when cumulative taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months; below this threshold the WFOE may remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer subject to the statutory simplified levy rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China has mandated the Fully Digitalised Electronic Invoice (FDEI) reform. All VAT invoices must be issued through the STA e-Tax/e-invoice service platform or through an STA-certified enterprise e-invoicing API; each invoice must carry an invoice code, encryption signature, and anti-fraud QR code in the standard OFD/XML data format. Issued invoice data is transmitted in real time to STA's Golden Tax Project Phase IV central data platform, where it is automatically reconciled with VAT returns, customs export declarations, bank payment data, and foreign-exchange receipt data. Newly established WFOEs are expected to adopt fully digitalised e-invoicing from inception; legacy tax-control devices remain permitted only during the express transitional period allowed by local STA.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For export of goods, 0% VAT and input-VAT refund apply if the goods are physically exported from China under customs supervision, the supply is made by a VAT general taxpayer, a valid China Customs export declaration is filed, the goods actually leave Chinese customs territory, and the export proceeds are repatriated and received through lawful foreign-exchange settlement channels. For cross-border services, including the dry leasing of aircraft engines to a non-resident lessee, zero-rating or exemption is available only if the service falls within the catalogue of cross-border taxable services under Caishui [2016] No. 36 and is 'fully consumed outside China', evidenced by the lessee being located outside China, the aircraft engine being operated wholly outside Chinese territory, and payment being received from outside China; operating leases of tangible movable assets are not presumptively zero-rated, so the taxpayer must verify whether the precise service is classified as zero-rated or exempt, because only zero-rated categories restore input VAT while exempt categories do not.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration issued by the General Administration of Customs, bearing the customs declaration number, commodity HS code, value, and customs release record.
Commercial invoice and packing list issued by the WFOE describing the aircraft engine, quantity, unit price, total consideration, and terms of the lease or sale.
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical movement of the aircraft engine out of Chinese customs territory.

Foreign-exchange receipt voucher from a PRC-designated bank, comprising the cross-border income declaration and/or bank currency-receipt memorandum, evidencing lawful repatriation of the lease rental or sale consideration.

Executed export contract or aircraft-engine lease agreement, together with aircraft-engine registration and technical documents, evidencing the cross-border transaction and the location of use outside China.

For zero-rated cross-border services, a tax-residency certificate of the non-resident lessee and a signed lessee declaration confirming that the aircraft engine will remain and operate entirely outside China.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: STA and China Customs electronically cross-check e-invoice data, VAT returns, customs export declarations, logistics documents, and bank foreign-exchange receipt records. If zero-rating is claimed without a genuine export or offshore consumption, without physical departure from China, or without foreign-exchange repatriation within the statutory period, STA will revoke the zero-rating, reassess VAT output tax, and impose daily late-payment surcharge at 0.05% of the underpaid tax from the original due date. Fraudulent export declarations or fraudulent export-tax-refund claims are punishable under Article 66 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Administration of Tax Collection by confiscation of the refund fraudulently obtained and a fine of one to five times the amount wrongly claimed; criminal liability may arise under PRC Criminal Law for the crime of fraudulently obtaining export tax refunds, with imprisonment and additional fines. The WFOE may also be retroactively reclassified as a small-scale taxpayer or lose export-tax-refund qualification, and prior zero-rated supplies may be clawed back within the statutory assessment period, generally three years, extended or unlimited where there is evasion or fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a current-account convertible regime for trade and services while retaining administrative controls over capital-account flows. The WFOE may freely accept and settle foreign currency lease rentals, pay cross-border service fees, and remit distributable profits after tax, provided that SAFE reporting, tax withholdings, customs declarations, and anti-money-laundering controls are satisfied. The RMB does not float freely; the onshore daily band is managed by the PBOC against a currency basket, and SAFE supervises all foreign exchange transactions through the bank reporting system. Capital inflows such as equity injections, shareholder loans, and external debt require FDI registration, foreign debt registration or quota approval, and an onshore capital account before conversion. Profit remittance, although current-account in principle, is deferred until the statutory annual audit, and the bank requires tax clearance certificates, board resolutions, audited financial statements, and supporting lease contracts. Surrender of export and service proceeds is no longer mandatory, but lease revenues must be repatriated to China and credited to a domestic foreign-exchange current account within the statutory reporting periods; funds can be retained in foreign currency or converted at the operator's election. The practical result is that the WFOE treasury must maintain segregated capital and current accounts, dual bookkeeping, and robust documentation for every FX movement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For goods exports, foreign currency export proceeds must be repatriated to China and received into an onshore foreign-exchange account within 180 days of the customs export declaration. For service trade such as aircraft engine dry leasing, the proceeds must be repatriated and reported within the applicable SAFE reporting window, generally 180 days from the invoice or contractual due date. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the WFOE may retain 100 percent in foreign currency or convert into RMB at market rates through a licensed bank. However, the entire amount must be captured on the bank's SAFE reporting system and supported by the lease agreement, invoice, and proof of actual service delivery; any late repatriation, netting without approval, or unreported foreign receipt triggers enhanced scrutiny and penalties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Non-viable as a primary treasury rail. China does not grant offshore fintech EMI or digital bank licenses for local onboarding, and a cross-border digital EMI cannot open a CNAPS account, settle RMB directly, or accept the WFOE as a client in a banking capacity. Such platforms are legally barred from servicing mainland entities as deposit-taking institutions. They may act only as ancillary payment facilitators if the underlying funds are held by a licensed onshore commercial bank and the EMI has a registered commercial presence in China; even then, the official SWIFT/CIPS banking rails and SAFE reporting remain mandatory for capital injections and lease-related cross-border flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is generally mandatory for the legal representative, actual controller, and at least one authorized signatory when the WFOE account is first opened. The bank conducts a face-to-face interview, verifies original corporate seals, checks director identities, and signs account opening documents on-site. A fully remote consular proxy opening is not a statutory right; some banks may accept a notarized power of attorney with Chinese consular legalization only after the legal representative has previously completed a high-definition video KYC and biometric verification. In practice, hybrid or video onboarding is narrow, bank-specific, and does not eliminate the bank's right to demand a subsequent physical meeting for enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or high-risk UBO chain involving offshore intermediate holding vehicles, nominee directors, and opaque source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A granular ownership diagram through each intermediary, audited financial statements of the immediate parent and ultimate shareholder, certificates of incorporation and good standing, registers of directors and shareholders, notarized passports, a bank reference letter from the home-country correspondent bank, independent source-of-wealth reports covering the funding for the WFOE equity contribution, and sworn declarations confirming that no UBO is a politically exposed person or sanctioned counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aircraft engine asset provenance and related-party acquisition lacking independent valuation or clear title history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Engine serial number and manufacturer records, title registry extracts from the applicable civil aviation authority or FAA register, full chain of bills of sale, the original lease or acquisition agreement, an independent aviation appraisal report, hull and engine insurance certificates, maintenance and service history logs, export/import permits, customs declarations, and a written statement explaining the commercial purpose of any related-party transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure, adverse media, or payment routing through shell or intermediary banks when the proposed foreign lessee or airline is involved
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions screening reports from a reputable screening provider, a complete lessee and end-user KYC pack, audited lessee financials, a tax residence certificate, the fully executed dry lease agreement with arm's-length pricing clauses, explanation of the route of funds with supporting SWIFT pre-advices, and a legal opinion confirming that the lessee is not owned by or acting for any OFAC/EU/UN sanctioned party.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious capital injection pattern or mismatch between the lease contract economics and transaction size, frequency, or FX purpose codes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of shareholder loan or equity subscription agreements, SAFE FDI registration documents, the bank's foreign debt registration certificates if applicable, a capital verification report issued by a licensed Chinese CPA, board resolutions approving each remittance, full bank statements of the originating shareholder account, pro-forma invoices, the underlying lease contracts, and a cash-flow forecast demonstrating that the transaction size and timing are consistent with the aviation leasing business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires completion of SAFE FDI foreign-exchange registration with a unique FDI code; injection by each foreign shareholder from its own bank account via SWIFT MT103 using the stated purpose of equity investment or registered capital contribution for the WFOE; crediting of funds to the onshore Foreign Exchange Capital Account in the WFOE's name; authenticity review by the receiving bank before conversion of funds into RMB; negative-list compliance screening where applicable; engagement of a licensed Chinese CPA to issue a capital verification report within the statutory capital contribution period; and retention of the SWIFT advice, bank credit slip, CPA report, SAFE receipts, and corporate resolutions for audit.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: For aircraft engine purchase, maintenance, and lease-related payments, the preferred clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for direct expense remittances, SWIFT MT700 commercial letters of credit for large engine acquisitions, and documentary collections such as documents against payment or documents against acceptance for settlements where counterparty trust is moderate. All outbound current-account remittances must be supported by the underlying lease or sale contract, invoice, tax withholding certificates for non-resident enterprise income tax and relevant VAT or customs taxes, and the appropriate SAFE trade or service payment code. Lease rents paid to an overseas owner must be reported under the service-trade remittance category for operating lease rent and cannot be netted against incoming lease receivables without a separate SAFE offset approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY/USD FX forward contracts for firm lease receivables and payables, with a SAFE-licensed onshore bank and genuine underlying aviation lease exposure.
Cross-currency swaps with onshore banks for long-term fixed-to-floating or floating-to-fixed conversion of USD-denominated engine rental streams into CNY debt-service cash flows.
FX options purchased from an onshore bank for hedging lease-payment volatility; options writing requires documented economic risk, bank approval, and SAFE-compliant underlying exposure.

Non-deliverable forward overlays are not permissible inside the onshore WFOE; an offshore parent may hedge through the offshore NDF market for consolidated exposure, but the onshore entity cannot record NDF settlements without SAFE authorization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report (annual return) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local municipal/district market supervision administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 of each calendar year following the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If not publicized by June 30, the entity is placed on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations within 10 working days; publication and application can remove it, but continued non-compliance for three years moves it to the Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List, triggers joint credit restrictions on the legal representative, and may be followed by administrative revocation of the business license if the enterprise ceases operations or fails to maintain lawful corporate existence. False or concealed annual report information may attract fines of RMB 10,000-RMB 30,000 under market regulation rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement and Final Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) competent tax authority at the WFOE's registration and business location
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the year following the calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax (approximately 18.25% per annum); failure to file within the deadline exposes the company to a fine of up to RMB 10,000 (RMB 2,000 in ordinary cases) and possible 50%-500% penalty for underpayment or evasion; non-filing may freeze tax collection powers, restrict credit and export, and escalate to asset enforcement by the tax authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report for the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the Foreign Investment Comprehensive Information Reporting System / provincial commerce department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or false submission triggers an order to rectify within a prescribed period; continued default can lead to administrative fines up to RMB 300,000, inclusion in enterprise credit or discredit information systems, and restrictions in government procurement, licensing and financing activities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual SAFE Foreign Direct Investment Equity Information Registration (annual stock of foreign investor equity and financial position filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the Foreign Exchange Digital Administration Platform / SAFE local branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing places the WFOE in SAFE's non-compliant foreign exchange monitoring records; cross-border foreign exchange receipts, payments and capital account services may be suspended until the filing is rectified, and administrative fines or foreign exchange regulatory penalties may be imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory audited financial statements with a PRC-licensed CPA audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders, board of directors and corporate records; the audit report is used to support the SAMR annual report, CIT annual return and MOFCOM/SAFE foreign investment filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit completed and audited financial statements approved by the shareholders' meeting no later than June 30; prudent completion date is April 30 to allow May 31 CIT filing and June 30 annual filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a statutory audit is a breach of PRC Company Law audit provisions; it may render annual filings legally false, disqualify tax benefits or transfer-pricing documentation protections, give shareholders inspection and damages rights, and subject the entity or responsible individuals to supervisory orders, fines and adverse credit findings if audited reports are demanded by SAMR, tax or banking counterparties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social insurance contribution base declaration and housing fund annual adjustment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local municipal or district Human Resources and Social Security Bureau and local Housing Provident Fund Management Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Usually January 1 through March 31 for the annual base declaration in most municipalities; exact local window varies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpaid social insurance accrues daily late fees of 0.05% and may attract fines up to three times the overdue amount; false declarations may result in labor inspection orders, administrative penalties, and restrictions on corporate credit.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under PRC Company Law, every limited liability company and every one-person limited liability company must have its financial reports audited each financial year by a lawfully qualified accounting firm; there is no quantitative below-threshold exemption for a mainland WFO

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China's national headline Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) rate is 25%. A qualifying Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) can reduce EIT to 15% under the High and New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) regime, the Western Region development incentive, Hainan Free Trade Port, or certain Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macau Greater Bay Area preferential city programs. R&D expenditures generally enjoy a 100% additional deduction (200% total deduction) if the activities qualify as R&D. Small low-profit enterprises may benefit from reduced effective rates through the taxable-income threshold; technology transfer income within RMB 5 million is exempt and amounts above that threshold are taxed at 50% of the normal income inclusion, subject to conditions. China does not maintain a national patent box, but R&D deductions and HNTE regimes serve as de facto IP incentives. Loss carryforward is 5 years for ordinary taxpayers, extended to 10 years for HNTE and technology-oriented SME status taxpayers, subject to the Chinese tax administration's rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000, the Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return for Resident Enterprises (A-class), and associated schedules including A105000 (tax adjustment), A105080 (asset depreciation), A106000 (loss carryover), A107010 (tax-exempt and reduced income), A108010 (foreign tax credit), and the related-party transaction reporting forms G100000-series, all filed through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly provisional EIT filings/payments required for all resident WFOEs.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual EIT return must be filed within 5 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year WFOE the deadline is 31 May of the following year. Quarterly provisional EIT returns are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter under Articles 54 and 55 of the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from aircraft engine dry-leasing, lease rental invoiced to airlines, late fees, and ancillary leasing income, stated exclusive of VAT and surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only China-source rental income. Under EIT Law Article 7, rent paid by a Chinese enterprise or income from property used in China is China-source; for an engine physically deployed outside Chinese territory, maintain lessee tax residency certificates, flight logs, and parking and usage records to support exclusion from Chinese EIT. Where the lessee is a non-resident airline, obtain documentary evidence that the engine's core operational location is outside China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to the leasing activity: capitalised engine acquisition cost depreciated under tax rules, maintenance and overhaul expenditure, insurance, delivery and positioning costs, and any lease-in rent if the WFOE is a sub-lessor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use statutory tax depreciation lives for aircraft equipment, generally a minimum of 10 years, and complete Schedule A105080 for differences between book and tax depreciation. If the engine is imported from a non-resident seller, the purchase price is not subject to dividend/interest/royalty withholding, but import VAT and customs duties should be capitalised; if the contract is worded as payment for the right to use equipment, certain treaties might recharacterise a part as a royalty, so the dry-lease substance must be preserved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible Chinese taxes and surcharges other than EIT: urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, stamp duty, property tax and land-use tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT is not an EIT deduction to the extent input VAT is separately credited. For cross-border engine leases, import VAT and tariffs are not ordinary deductions but form part of asset cost or deductible expense only where permitted. Stamp duty on loan, lease and service contracts should be settled and documented to support deductions of related financing and service costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales and marketing expenses, commissions, advertising, tendering costs and business development incurred to place engines with airlines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commissions paid to non-resident brokers or agents may be treated as China-source service fees and are subject to 10% withholding tax unless treaty relief applies. The WFOE should retain binding agency agreements, proof of actual service performance, and an arm's-length commission benchmark; payments to a related-party marketer without substance are likely to be disallowed and recharacterised as a dividend distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management, legal, audit, travel, rent, office depreciation and general corporate overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Parent-company recharges or group service fees must satisfy the benefit test, be supported by contracts, detailed invoices and work-product evidence, and be priced on an arm's-length basis. Fees paid to a non-resident parent for stewardship or duplicate services are non-deductible; if the payment is made to a related party, the WFOE must prepare contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation and may need to disclose the transaction in the annual related-party reporting forms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bank interest, loan fees, guarantee fees, foreign-exchange losses and other financing costs of the WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a non-resident shareholder or affiliate is deductible only to the extent of the thin-capitalisation debt-to-equity safe harbour, generally 2:1 for non-financial enterprises and 5:1 for financial enterprises; excess interest is non-deductible and may be recharacterised as a dividend subject to 10% withholding. For cross-border loans, document the actual loan agreement, interest-rate benchmark, and beneficial ownership certificate; on interest payment to a non-resident, withhold at the 10% statutory rate or reduced treaty rate under the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bad-debt losses and impairment of receivables from lessees and finance-lease assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses recognised under tax law, supported by evidence of uncollectability, are deductible. A waiver or forgiveness of a receivable owed by a non-resident affiliate is generally viewed as a capital contribution, dividend distribution or transfer-pricing adjustment rather than a deductible expense; complete the relevant adjustment schedule and preserve board minutes and collection efforts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8 – Fair Value Changes and Derivative Gains
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mark-to-market gains and losses on derivatives, foreign-exchange hedges and financial instruments used to manage lease rate or fuel exposure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the underlying lease exposure and hedge relationship so that unrealised gains and losses are properly reported; payments of hedging premiums to non-resident counterparties may constitute interest or service fees subject to withholding; losses on a transaction lacking economic substance will be disregarded under GAAR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend income, deposit interest, equity investment disposal gains and fund distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from a Chinese resident enterprise may be exempt from EIT when the shareholding qualifies as direct investment between Chinese resident enterprises under Article 26 of the EIT Law. Dividends received from non-resident subsidiaries are taxable, with a foreign tax credit available. Outbound dividends paid by the WFOE to a non-resident shareholder are never deductible and are subject to 10% withholding, reducible only under a DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit before income tax expense, prepared under Chinese Accounting Standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the return to the audited local statutory financial statements. Disclose all cross-border related-party balances, including lease receivables, shareholder loans, accrued interest and unpaid royalties, in the related-party transaction attachment; failure to file the related-party reporting schedule may trigger penalties and transfer-pricing audits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted for permanent differences, temporary differences, transfer-pricing adjustments, tax-exempt income, non-deductible expenses and loss carryovers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible management fees, entertainment expenses, overhead allocated by a non-resident head office, excess interest, and hidden equity distributions embedded in related-party payments. Apply the 5-year general loss carryover or, where eligible, the 10-year carryover for HNTE and technology-oriented small enterprises. Cross-border dry-leasing transactions with a foreign parent must be benchmarked at arm's length; any net adjustment increases taxable income and may trigger a special tax adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 20/33 – Tax Payable and Foreign Tax Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: EIT liability calculated at 25% on taxable income, reduced by quarterly prepayments, transitional credits, tax incentive credits and foreign tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim a foreign tax credit only for income taxes paid abroad on foreign-source income included in the Chinese taxable base; outbound dividends are not subject to Chinese EIT at the distributing WFOE level. If a foreign shareholder's treaty relief is denied, the WFOE as withholding agent remains responsible for the additional 10% withholding tax, plus interest and penalties, unless the contractual arrangement shifts the liability and the WFOE can substantiate proper withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing of an EIT return is penalised under Articles 62 and 63 of the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection (LATC), generally a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, and up to RMB 50,000 for serious failure. Underpaid tax carries a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%; deliberate false returns or concealment that result in underpayment attract a penalty of 50%-500% of the additional tax, and criminal tax evasion can be prosecuted under Criminal Law Article 201 with imprisonment up to 7 years where the amount and ratio are large. Directors, legal representatives and actual controllers who caused a false filing can be blacklisted under the social credit system, become judgment debtors, and be restricted from leaving China.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% of the gross dividend paid to a non-resident enterprise shareholder when the dividend is China-source and the recipient has no permanent establishment in China, under PRC EIT Law Articles 3(3), 27(4) and 37. The rate can be reduced, most commonly to 5% for a corporate shareholder resident in a treaty jurisdiction that beneficially owns at least 25% of the equity, under the relevant DTA, including the China-Hong Kong double tax arrangement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The WFOE, as withholding agent, must apply the treaty rate in the withholding and payment process under SAT Public Notice 2015 No. 60. The procedure requires the non-resident shareholder to provide, before or at the time of dividend payment, a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC
